transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~55m
Attendees: Lena (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Mark (Peloton CTO), Ava (Peloton SRE), Luis (Peloton ML)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Peloton is evaluating moving latency-sensitive customer-facing generation from OpenAI hosted to Redwood Dedicated/Private. Key concerns: eval parity, compatibility with existing prompts and tooling (vLLM/TGI), tokenization differences, latency p99, KV cache behavior, encryption/KMS, SSO, and long-term cost model. Agreed to share pricing, security docs, and run perf/quality POC.

[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros — I'm Lena on the AE side, Samir is our solutions engineer.
[00:18] Mark: Hey, Mark here, CTO at Peloton Labs. Ava and Luis from infra and ML are here too.
[00:25] Samir: Great, thanks. Super high level — you're currently on OpenAI hosted for all generation, is that right?
[00:33] Mark: Yeah we run a mix, mostly gpt-4-ish endpoints, with fallback to smaller models. We're seeing cost creep and occasional rate limits during peak live sessions. Looking into Redwood Dedicated to get predictable throughput and also explore private deployments for compliance.
[00:50] Ava: Also, we have an SSO / SAML requirement, SOC2 plus data residency for EU customers, and we need audit logs.
[00:58] Lena: Totally. We'll cover hosted vs dedicated vs private, and Samir will do the deep-dive on performance and compatibility.

--- Discovery / qualification ---
[01:15] Samir: A few clarifying Qs — what's your current QPS and typical prompt sizes? Any batching already?
[01:25] Luis: For our live product, avg prompt 220 tokens, but some sessions spike to 1.2k. Peak QPS ~45 reqs/sec with bursts. We do some client-side batching for embeddings but not for chat generation.
[01:40] Samir: Helpful. What's your success criteria for migration? Latency targets, cost targets, and quality parity?
[01:48] Mark: Latency p95 under 200ms for simple completion endpoints; p99 as low as we can get, ideally <500ms. Cost needs to be at least 30% better than current per-token spend, or equivalent with better SLOs. And evaluation parity — we can't regress on metrics in our regression test suite.
[02:05] Samir: Got it. And compliance: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS for key management, VPC peering for Dedicated/Private?
[02:12] Ava: Yes, VPC peering or private connectivity required for Dedicated; Private deployment even better if we need on-prem.

--- Technical deep-dive: inference stack compatibility ---
[03:00] Samir: On the compatibility side — you mentioned you run some vLLM locally for dev and TGI in a staged setup. Are you tied to the OpenAI API contract for production?
[03:12] Luis: Our app integrates with OpenAI-ish endpoints and we've built some wrappers to handle streaming and function calls. We want to minimize code changes. Also curious about kv-cache behavior — we've been relying on vLLM's cache to keep context warm.
[03:28] Samir: Redwood's API supports OpenAI-compatible endpoints for common patterns (chat/completions/embeddings) but there are differences. We maintain a model catalog and runtime that can run Open weights and OpenAPI-like wrappers. On KV cache: our runtime exposes persistent KV caching semantics and supports prefix caching; implementation differs under the hood vs vLLM but we can match the observable behavior.
[03:50] Mark: When you say "match," do you mean exact tokenization and logits parity or just similar outputs? Our eval suite is strict — small output deltas can fail.
[03:59] Samir: Important distinction. We aim for eval parity at the application level: we run the same model weights and comparable quantization to get similar outputs. But tiny differences can occur due to different tokenizers, decoding seeds, and kernel optimizations. For strict parity, we suggest running an eval parity job during POC with your prompt set and measuring delta.
[04:20] Luis: So is there an official flow for that? We currently use vLLM for batch evals.
[04:26] Samir: Yes — we provide a benchmark harness and scripts. We'll share the template; you can run against Redwood Dedicated and compare to OpenAI baseline. We'll also instrument token-level diffs and scoring.

--- Performance and runtime questions ---
[05:00] Mark: On latency — how does Redwood Dedicated achieve low p99s? Concerned about batching increasing tail latency.
[05:08] Samir: Two levers: smart routing to avoid oversubscription and continuous batching with latency SLOs. Our runtime prioritizes low-latency lanes (small seq lengths) and moves larger jobs to background queues. We also have KV cache to avoid recomputing prefixes. For tight p95/p99 we can reserve capacity and enable low-latency execution paths (less batching, more prewarmed workers).
[05:34] Ava: Does Dedicated let us pin node types and guarantee capacity?
[05:38] Lena: Yes Dedicated is reserved GPU pools; you can pick instance profiles, configure autoscale/burst policies, and get SLA-backed latency/uptime targets dependent on commit level.
[05:48] Mark: What about quantization? We need to run smaller profiles for cost, but worried about quality regressions.
[05:55] Samir: Redwood supports multiple quantization profiles (8-bit, 4-bit QAT-ish flows) and we recommend running a model quality sweep as part of rollout. The Optimize tool suggests profiles per workload. We'll include recommended profiles based on your evals.

--- Security / Compliance ---
[07:00] Ava: For keys and logs — do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and full audit logs?
[07:08] Samir: Yes. For Private we can integrate with your HSM/KMS and for Dedicated we support bring-your-own-key via KMS integrations. We provide audit logs for requests and administrative actions, retention configurable as an add-on.
[07:21] Ava: And SSO/SAML + RBAC?
[07:25] Lena: Yes, SSO/SAML plus granular RBAC is supported in Console. We'll share docs and a network diagram.

--- Migration constraints and tooling ---
[08:00] Mark: Migration-wise: we run function-calling and streaming heavily. Any gotchas for streaming compatibility?
[08:07] Samir: We support streaming and function/tool calling. The streaming chunk format is slightly different from OpenAI's in edge cases; most SDKs handle it, but we'll validate with your integration.
[08:18] Luis: On cost — how granular are chargebacks / per-route costs? We need to map costs to product features.
[08:25] Lena: Console gives token-level breakdowns by route/model, plus per-token unit cost. You can export usage for internal chargebacks.

--- Benchmarks & POC design ---
[09:00] Samir: Proposal for POC: 1) share prompt set + baseline outputs (you run on OpenAI or provide logs), 2) Redwood runs parity benchmarks on Dedicated nodes with recommended quantization, 3) measure latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput, and output similarity. We can also run a small canary with live traffic behind a routed policy.
[09:25] Mark: Timeline? We want to be live before summer launch mid-June ideally. Is that realistic?
[09:33] Samir: With dedicated sizing and a POC starting now, 6-8 weeks to production is realistic — depends on your infra approvals for VPC peering and KMS signoff.

--- Specific questions from Peloton ---
[12:00] Luis: Do you support our internal vLLM custom tokenizer tweaks? We have a tokenization preprocessor that rewrites inputs.
[12:10] Samir: We can accommodate upstream preprocessors; tokenizer changes might affect parity but we can run the exact same pipeline inside the POC to match behavior.
[12:20] Ava: For network connectivity — is dedicated traffic egress from Redwood or still proxied through your control plane? We need to keep data within our VPC.
[12:28] Lena: Dedicated supports VPC peering and private control plane options; logs and model weights can be configured per deployment mode. For strict data residency, Private on-prem or VPC-hosted private control plane is recommended.

--- Objections and tradeoffs ---
[15:00] Mark: Biggest hesitation is regression risk and the engineering effort to switch. Also we rely on OpenAI's content filters; what's Redwood's stance on safety pipelines?
[15:12] Samir: We have built-in moderation hooks and customers can bring their filters or use our prebuilt ones. For regressions, the POC covers eval parity — if we can't match thresholds, we won't proceed to cutover. We try to reduce code churn via API compatibility and SDKs.

--- Pricing and contractual ---
[18:00] Lena: Pricing model: Dedicated is commit-based reserved capacity (monthly/annual). Host pays per-instance reserved pool with optional overage. We'll send a sizing/pricing spreadsheet after today's sizing follow-ups.
[18:12] Mark: Do you offer short-term trials or credits for POC?
[18:16] Lena: Yes, we can provide a POC credit package and time-limited reserved pool for evaluation.

--- Demo notes / references ---
[22:00] Samir: I'll drop links after the call: benchmark template, migration runbook, security whitepaper, and the Dedicated config sheet.

--- Closing — Recap & next steps ---
[50:00] Lena: Quick recap: Peloton to run eval parity benchmarking during POC, Redwood to provide pricing and security docs, schedule a follow-up POC planning call with Samir + Peloton infra. Action items recorded.
[50:18] Mark: Sounds good. We'll get the prompt set and logs to you and schedule infra sync.
[50:25] Ava: I'll raise the VPC peering request internally and aim to have network contacts on the next call.
[50:33] Luis: I'll prepare the 1k request sample and full regression suite output.
[50:40] Lena: Great — we'll circulate notes and the spreadsheets. Thanks everyone.
[50:48] Mark: Thanks all.
